PRODUCT_KIND.question: Is what you place on the market hardware, software, or an online service?
PRODUCT_KIND.why_we_ask: The CRA covers products: hardware and software, including a cloud backend that your product needs in order to work. A purely online service with no product behind it is not covered.

MARKET_STATUS.question: Where is the product in its life on the EU market?
MARKET_STATUS.why_we_ask: The CRA applies to products supplied on the EU market. If you plan to sell in the EU, we answer for the moment the product goes on sale. Showing a prototype at a fair, or using something only inside your own company, is not supplying it.

COMMERCIAL_ACTIVITY.question: Is it supplied in the course of a commercial activity, whether paid or free of charge?
COMMERCIAL_ACTIVITY.why_we_ask: The CRA only covers products supplied as part of a business activity. Giving something away for free can still count: what matters is whether you earn from it in some way, for example by charging for support, for a platform around it, or by requiring users' personal data. Truly non-commercial projects, such as most volunteer open-source work, are outside.

legal_basis.quote: in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge

text.heading: Article 3: Definitions

parts.text: ‘making available on the market’ means the supply of a product with digital elements for distribution or use on the Union market
in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge

legal_basis.quote: Supply in the course of a commercial activity might be characterised not only by charging a price for a product with digital elements, but also by charging a price for technical support services where this does not serve only the recuperation of actual costs, by an intention to monetise

DATA_INTERFACE_PRESENT.question: Does the product have any way to exchange data at all: network, radio, cable, USB, memory card, or a software interface?
DATA_INTERFACE_PRESENT.why_we_ask: The CRA covers products that can exchange data with something else. If your product has no way at all to exchange data (no network, radio, cable, USB, card slot or software interface), it is outside the CRA.

CONNECTION_INTENDED.question: Is the product intended to exchange data with another device or network, directly or indirectly?
CONNECTION_INTENDED.why_we_ask: What counts is whether exchanging data is part of how the product is meant to be used. It does not have to be the internet: a USB cable, Bluetooth, or a link through another device all count.

MEDICAL_STATUS.question: Is it CE-marked as a medical or in vitro diagnostic device, or does it have a medical purpose without being certified as one?
MEDICAL_STATUS.why_we_ask: Medical devices are excluded only if the medical device rules actually apply to them. A product with a medical purpose that is not certified as a medical device raises a question about those rules, which this tool cannot answer.

SPARE_PART.why_we_ask: A spare part that replaces an identical component, made to the same specifications, is excluded. A replacement with different or improved specifications is a product in its own right.

PURPOSE_SCREEN.question: What is your product mainly for? Tick all that apply, or none.
PURPOSE_SCREEN.why_we_ask: To say a product is not in a listed category, the tool has to rule that category out. Tick what your product is mainly for, not every function it has: a smart lock that has an app with a login is not mainly for storing passwords.

info.title: Hypervisors and container runtime systems that support virtualised execution of operating systems and similar environments
named_products: This category includes but is not limited to type 1 hypervisors (bare metal), type 2 hypervisors (hosted on an operating system) and hybrid hypervisors.
info.description: Hypervisors are software products with digital elements that abstract and/or allocate computing resources and enable the execution, management and orchestration of virtual machines that are logically separated from each other and/or from the physical hardware. Hypervisors may run directly on hardware (bare metal), on top of an operating system, or within another virtual machine (nested virtualisation). In the context of this category of products, a virtual machine is a software-defined logical separation of a computing environment, which includes a virtualised set of hardware resources (e.g. CPU, memory, storage, network interfaces) and typically hosts its own operating system. This category includes but is not limited to type 1 hypervisors (bare metal), type 2 hypervisors (hosted on an operating system) and hybrid hypervisors. Container runtime systems are software products with digital elements that manage the execution and lifecycle of containers running on a single host operating system as isolated processes, allocating resources and allowing the management and orchestration of individual containers. In the context of this category of products, a container is a software-based execution environment that encapsulates one or more software components and their dependencies in a single package, enabling it to run independently and consistently.

VIRTUALISATION_TYPE.question: Does it run virtual machines or containers? Which describes it best?
VIRTUALISATION_TYPE.why_we_ask: Hypervisors and container runtimes are Class II products. A tool that only schedules containers across machines, without running them itself, is a case the law does not clearly settle.

legal_basis.quote: enable the execution, management and orchestration of virtual machines

text.heading: Annex, Class II, point 1: Hypervisors and container runtime systems that support virtualised execution of operating systems and similar environments

parts.text: Hypervisors are software products with digital elements that abstract and/or allocate computing resources and
enable the execution, management and orchestration of virtual machines

that are logically separated from each other and/or from the physical hardware. Hypervisors may run directly on hardware (bare metal), on top of an operating system, or within another virtual machine (nested virtualisation). In the context of this category of products, a virtual machine is a software-defined logical separation of a computing environment, which includes a virtualised set of hardware resources (e.g. CPU, memory, storage, network interfaces) and typically hosts its own operating system. This category includes but is not limited to type 1 hypervisors (bare metal), type 2 hypervisors (hosted on an operating system) and hybrid hypervisors. Container runtime systems are software products with digital elements that manage the execution and lifecycle of containers running on a single host operating system as isolated processes, allocating resources and allowing the management and orchestration of individual containers. In the context of this category of products, a container is a software-based execution environment that encapsulates one or more software components and their dependencies in a single package, enabling it to run independently and consistently.

protect a connected network or system from unauthorized access by monitoring and restricting data communication traffic
